teams.heading: Fiji Rugby parted ways with Mick Byrne in April by mutual agreement
teams.body: In April, Fiji Rugby and Mick Byrne parted ways "by mutual agreement", leaving the Flying Fijians looking for a new coach 18 months before the Rugby World Cup. Byrne had been in charge since 2024, after a spell at Fijian Drua, and his tenure brought wins over Scotland, Wales and Japan. AFP reported he appeared to have a difference of opinion with management over future plans. Byrne said he had been honoured to work with the Flying Fijians players and staff.

lead.why: It is the only shortlist item about the men's Flying Fijians rather than Sevens, league or past history, and the fact-check flagged it for correct dating, so it is the one story here that can run once

teams.heading: England lock Alex Coles scores and plays wing in Northampton's 71-48 win
teams.body: Alex Coles popped up on the wing for Northampton, made metres, trucked hard in the tight exchanges, ran the lineout and scored a try in the 71-48 win over Bath. Planet Rugby's winners list says his form has carried on from the end of last season into the new campaign, and that it will leave Steve Borthwick beaming. Coles's wing cameo is a useful reminder of his range for November.

teams.heading: Galthié's France went to Christchurch without its biggest stars, Dupont included
teams.body: Ahead of the July Nations Championship opener against New Zealand, coverage from early July reported that Fabien Galthié's touring squad left out Antoine Dupont, Romain Ntamack, Thomas Ramos, Grégory Alldritt and Louis Bielle-Biarrey. Many of the absences were tied to player workload after the long Top 14 season, leaving France to lean on a younger group against one of the toughest road opponents in international rugby.

teams.heading: Italy sit 11th of 12 after three defeats, conceding 131 points
teams.body: Italy go into the weekend 11th of 12 in the log after three defeats from three matches, scoring 37 points and conceding 131. Points difference stands at -94. teams.heading: World Rugby loses bid to strike out brain injury claims
teams.body: The legal action over concussion and brain injuries in rugby remains open, with claimants reported to face a £2.8m legal bill to continue the case. Earlier, in August, World Rugby and UK bodies lost a bid to have the brain injury cases thrown out of court. No settlement or further ruling has been reported since, so the case stays open until the claimants settle their fees or it is resolved.

teams.heading: Tommy Reffell presses Wales starting case with breakdown display for Leicester
teams.body: In the Premiership, Leicester flanker Tommy Reffell made the strongest case for a Wales starting shirt in Friday's 38-31 win over Gloucester, according to Planet Rugby's winners-and-losers verdict. He was a nuisance at the breakdown all evening, and his try-saving tackle on Will Joseph on 65 minutes was vital. The display was framed as pressing his claim ahead of Wales' November Nations Championship block.

teams.heading: Mario Ledesma returns as Los Pumas forwards coach through 2027 World Cup
teams.body: Mario Ledesma is back at Los Pumas as forwards coach until the end of the 2027 World Cup in Australia, the Argentine Rugby Union has confirmed. The former hooker won 84 Tests between 1996 and 2011 and coached Argentina from 2018 to 2022. "I am honoured and very grateful for the opportunity to work with Los Pumas again," Ledesma said. He and Shaun Edwards start work with the Pumas at the end of October, ahead of the November Nations Championship matches.

lead.why: It is the only angle in the pack that moves beyond the Edwards signing, with Mario Ledesma's return as forwards coach.

teams.heading: Wallabies cling to sixth in world rankings after All Blacks loss
teams.body: Eden Park cost the Wallabies more than a 50-19 scoreline: their World Rugby rating slipped from 85.55 to 84.89, leaving them sixth and just 0.11 ahead of Scotland in seventh. Had they won by more than 15 points, they could have moved into fourth, their highest ranking since November 2021, but that opportunity is gone. Another defeat in next Saturday's Sydney rematch would see them slip behind the Scots.

lead.why: It is a new development with real competitive stakes for Australia, and it is not a retelling of the Eden Park defeat that readers have already seen.

teams.heading: Hajime Shoji's League One reverses plan to treat naturalised players as foreign
teams.body: In late August, Japan Rugby League One, the domestic club competition, has backed down on registration rules that would have classed some Japanese-passport holders as foreign. Players who acquired Japanese citizenship, or applied, by May 2025 will now be treated as Japanese-born under the 2026-27 system, which begins in December. The original plan would have limited places for foreign-born players eligible to represent Japan. Shoji admitted: "We lacked communication with players who would be adversely affected by the changes."

lead.why: It is the only shortlisted item not already run on this tab, and it bears directly on who is eligible to play for Japan.

teams.heading: All Blacks close to 1.28 points behind Springboks in world rankings
teams.body: In World Rugby's men's rankings, New Zealand rose 0.66 to 91.81 after the 31-point Eden Park win over Australia, 1.28 behind the Springboks on 93.09. The gap stood at almost four points after the Springboks beat the Wallabies 3-1 in Rugby's Greatest Rivalry, and Australia stayed sixth on 84.89. Providing they get through next week's Sydney Test unscathed, Planet Rugby says the All Blacks may fancy finishing the year as the top-ranked side.

lead.why: The rankings shift is a new angle on the Bledisloe result, with the All Blacks closing on the Springboks, and it avoids repeating the match report and injury stories already run.

teams.heading: Springboks Hanekom and Moodie shine as Bulls thrash Lions 57-15 in URC
teams.body: In the United Rugby Championship, the Bulls beat the Lions 57-15 on Saturday, and the returning Springboks did much of the damage. Johan Ackermann started Grobbelaar, Steenekamp, Hanekom and Moodie, and all four stood out. Van Staden, Wiese, Louw and Pollard made their impact from the bench, with Pollard also slotting three conversions. The Bulls led 31-10 at half-time after a yellow card to Lions scrum-half Morne van den Berg.

lead.why: A fresh URC result, not the rankings or Pietersen selection already run, and it shows the returning Springboks making an immediate impact.
